result.summary:
I built seven staged modules on top of the 11 round-1 modules. There is now one zero-boundary-left-half (ZBL) development, and every glue theorem (b1–b5) is fully proved. All modules compile, and `import Ruliology` together with all seven imports compiles with no name clashes. 157 main theorems were checked with #print axioms, and each uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. A scan of the seven files finds no sorry, native_decide, admit, axiom, #eval or #print.

Encoding (A): the primary encoding is `zrow L t k` (depth k is position -k, depth 0 is the wall and is forced white at every time). It is reconmap's `zrow`, which is the same definition as the barriers' `z`. ProgA, monovariant, A1Reform and the barrier code were rewritten into it. The only remaining bridges are to other catalog encodings: `L_eq_zrow` and `Q01_iff_staged` (to the round-1 `Rule30DrivenLeft.L` and `Rule30PeriodTwo.Q01`), `left_half_is_zbl` (to `cell`), and `cell_eq_drv` (right half).

Modules and build times, measured one at a time with sb.sh:
- Rule30ZeroBoundary: 3.3 s
- Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripe: 17.3 s
- Rule30ZeroBoundarySmall: 15.9 s
- Rule30ZeroBoundaryBarriers: 3.2 s
- Rule30Ether: 4.6 s
- Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled: 0.6 s
- Rule30PeriodFourSkeleton: 3.3 s

The two slow modules are dominated by their decide +kernel checks. Run in parallel at load about 7 on 16 cores, they took the same time. Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled is a seventh module not in the suggested list; it holds b2 and b5.

Glue theorems:
- **(b1)** `C3 w` uses Rule30DrivenLeft.L driven by `wordAt (effWord w)`. `effWord_*` gives c' = 0000, 0010, 0110, and `colPattern` gives P_w = (0,*,0,1), (*,0,0,1), (*,0,0,1). The proofs `not_eventually_000x/0011/0111_of_C3` and `least_period_four_of_C3` go through `cell_eq_L_effective` and the skeleton theorems. The phase is (t−T)%4 in every one of them.
- **(b2)** `CQ01`, `CQ01_of_Q01`, and `no_eventual_period_two_of_CQ01` (any transient; the constant case goes through `Rule30PeriodTwo.normalize`, which uses `center_not_eventually_constant`).
- **(b3)** `col1_black_among_five` and `free_bits_no00_no11111`. The kernel check runs over 2^11 windows (columns 1..11), not 2^10, because the staged `col1_alt` needs k+2 cells.
- **(b4)** `Theta_eventually_stripe_iff`.
- **(b5)** `c7_eq_ether` (a shift of 4), `etherLeft_zbl`, `ether_col1_black`, `ether_free_bits`, and `ether_coupled_witness`. Also added: `etherLeft_eq_Theta`, `etherRight_drv`, and `trunc_not_left_half`, which shows the barrier witnesses are never a true left half.

Q01, CQ01, C3 w and Absorption w are still open. The theorems only prove implications from them.

Overlaps that remain: `Rule30PeriodTwo` keeps Int-indexed versions of `stripe_fixed`, `left_half_zero_driven` and `Q01`. That module is in the repo and was not modified; these are bridged by `L_eq_zrow` and `Q01_iff_staged`.

Checks are in integrate-r2/check/AllAx.lean and AllAx.out; scratch work is in integrate-r2/work.

Problem 1 of the Rule 30 Prize asks whether the center column c of rule 30 started from a single black cell is never eventually periodic. It is still open after two rounds. What is proved in Lean 4 is a set of unconditional partial results. The axioms of every cited theorem were re-printed in this pass, and only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound occur. The results are:
- Jen's theorem.
- No column is eventually constant.
- Masked and effective-boundary forms of Jen.
- The periods of the diagonals.
- The nine-black shield, with Theorems B, B′ and D.
- Three individually certified repeating words, a table of thirty more, and several infinite word families.
- The kernel-checked bound T + P ≥ 16359 on any eventual period P with transient T.
- The black-seed and white-seed centers are not both eventually periodic.

Eventual period 2 is reduced to two open conditions:
- Q01, a statement about the zero-boundary left half (ZBL). It is proved equivalent to three other forms: LR, bounded white runs, and "Φ(f) is never finitely supported".
- A weaker coupled condition CQ01 that also uses the right half.

Least period 4 is reduced to the Lean propositions Absorption(w) and C3(w); the second is built on Lean skeleton theorems for the right half. The CQ01 and C3 reductions, the no-11111 law and the ether facts were formalized by the parallel integration task. I compiled those seven staged modules from source and printed the axioms of all 335 of their theorems.

The ZBL under the period-2 constraint is proved conjugate to the full shift on its free bits. Its histories split into epochs, and stripe tails are absorbed.

Barrier theorems in Lean show three things:
- Finite abstractions, local rankings and edge automata cannot prove Q01. Their truncated-stripe witnesses violate the right-half constraint.
- Two-sided local rankings fail on truncations of the period-4 ether.
- Windows near the edge carry no information.

Computation finds no additive conservation law of small range.

Computations support the open hypotheses; each one is marked as cross-validated or not:
- Every ZBL start of width W ≤ 71 dies by time 2W + 8. Four independent codes agree up to W = 58, and W = 59–71 rests on one code, re-run here.
- Every finite right half tested enters the ether-and-wall family.
- The right half driven by an alternating center emits column-1 values in blocks 100 and 10000, with density 3/14.

The round-1 single-trap claim, low-complexity certificates and simple monovariants are refuted. What is missing is a global argument that a finitely supported configuration cannot sustain the coupled period-2 or period-4 constraints forever.

8 Relation to prior and third-party work
